name: Sunburst Electronics LLC
old_description: Sunburst Electronics was founded in 1976 and has operated continuously as an electronics manufacturing services provider for nearly five decades.
about:
Sunburst Electronics LLC was founded in 1976 in Erie, Pennsylvania. The company has operated continuously as an electronics manufacturing services provider for nearly five decades.

The company delivers full-service custom electronics contract manufacturing, specializing in printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), box builds, cable assemblies, and integrated high-reliability systems. Its capabilities span high-speed surface-mount (SMT) and through-hole assembly, BGA and micro-BGA placement, conformal coating (acrylic, silicone, urethane, parylene), potting, and comprehensive testing including AOI, X-ray inspection, flying-probe in-circuit test, vibration, burn-in, and environmental stress screening. Sunburst runs a designated prototype SMT line for rapid iteration and scales from prototype through high-volume production, offering both full turnkey and labor-only (customer-consigned) models.

Sunburst serves regulated and demanding sectors including medical technologies, defense, aerospace (aircraft and satellites), transportation, industrial controls, oil and gas, robotics, advanced computing, next-gen communications, and consumer electronics. Customers range from medical device OEMs requiring IPC/WHMA-A-620 compliant wire harnesses to aerospace programs needing ruggedized box builds engineered to MIL-STD-810 and MIL-STD-461.

Differentiators cited include global-to-regional sourcing transition to mitigate supply-chain risk, end-to-end lifecycle management from first build to end-of-life, and design-for-manufacturability reviews that compress time-to-market.

name: Sunrun
old_description: Since 2007, Sunrun solar energy systems have generated 25.6B kw hours of clean energy, helping enable the avoidance of an estimated 14.6 million metric tons of CO2e from entering the atmosphere.
about:
Sunrun was founded in 2007 and is headquartered in Essex Junction, Vermont. The company began with a focus on residential solar energy systems and has grown to serve homeowners across multiple states.

Sunrun designs, installs, and maintains solar panel and battery storage systems for homes. The company offers a subscription plan with predictable monthly payments, an equipment guarantee, and a monitoring app. To date, Sunrun has installed systems in over 1 million homes, generating 25.6 billion kilowatt-hours of clean energy and avoiding an estimated 14.6 million metric tons of CO2e. Customers have saved more than $1 billion on energy bills.

The company serves residential customers in states including California, Florida, Maryland, Nevada, New York, Texas, Hawaii, and Illinois. Its services cover system design, installation, maintenance, monitoring, and lease transfer through a dedicated portal. Sunrun partners with battery brands such as Tesla to provide storage solutions.

Sunrun emphasizes a comprehensive service model that includes repairs, maintenance, and monitoring, along with flexible payment options that require little to no money down. The company’s stated mission is to give homeowners control over their energy needs through an ecosystem of innovative products.

name: Sunshine Semiconductor, Inc.
old_description: Rebuilt and supported K&S Wire Bonders, Field Service, Training, and Installation — Nationwide
about:
Sunshine Semiconductor, Inc. operates from Pleasant View, Tennessee, where it has provided wire bonder support for more than 45 years. The company specializes in Kulicke and Soffa (K&S) equipment, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm rebuilds and fully supports K&S 4500 Series manual wire bonders, configuring them for ball, wedge, ribbon, bump, and TAB bonding applications. Its service portfolio covers on‑site troubleshooting, preventive maintenance, machine refurbishment, installation, operator training, process setup, and tooling recommendations. SunSemi also maintains a stock of legacy parts for older K&S platforms, including the 4100, 4500, 4700, and iBond 5000 series, and offers remote technical assistance from its Middle Tennessee base.

Customers span universities, research laboratories, defense contractors, aerospace companies, and microelectronics manufacturers across the United States. The company cites engagements in major technology corridors such as Silicon Valley, Boston’s Route 128, Dallas–Fort Worth, North Georgia, the Colorado Front Range, and Florida.

SunSemi emphasizes its depth of process knowledge — understanding both the machinery and the upstream and downstream factors that affect bonding reliability — as its primary differentiator. It positions its 45‑plus years of hands‑on K&S experience as a capability that generalist equipment dealers cannot match, particularly for keeping legacy bonders in stable, repeatable operation.

Sunwise Energy operates from Cherry Hill Township, New Jersey. The company's founding year and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

Its in-house teams handle site assessment, custom system design, permitting, installation, and utility interconnection. Sunwise reports having installed more than 50,000 solar panels across residential and commercial sites, with typical installation completed in one day once permits are approved.

Sunwise serves homeowners, businesses, and non-profit organizations primarily in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware. The company manages the full project lifecycle, including engineering, permitting, utility interconnection, and final inspection, aiming to meet deadlines such as the federal commercial tax credit cutoff of December 31, 2027.

Sunwise emphasizes that it uses no subcontractors, relying on its own trained technicians for installation and ongoing support. It offers $0-down financing options, real-time system monitoring, and assistance with incentives such as SRECs and MACRS depreciation for commercial clients.

name: Supercar System
about:
Supercar System operates from a factory at 5345 E North Belt Road in North Las Vegas, Nevada. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, nor are the names of its founders.

The company designs and builds F1-style six-speed sequential transmissions rated for up to 1,200 horsepower and 1,000 lb-ft of torque, with shift times quoted at 20 milliseconds. The units use 25 mm helical-cut gears that are case-hardened, precision-ground, and cryogenically treated, housed in a transverse stack for mass centralization. A limited-slip differential, integrated oil pump, and compatibility with GM LS and LT V8 blocks (via optional bolt-on bellhousing) round out the transmission package. Supercar System also lists "turnkey supercars and components" among its product offerings.

The transmissions target builders of high-performance street and track vehicles using GM V8 platforms, as well as integrators developing complete supercar programs. The quick-change rear-end ratios (3.75:1 ring and pinion) and multiple-orientation mounting suit both highway and circuit applications.

The company emphasizes gear strength, noise reduction, and compact packaging as core design goals, citing military-grade heat treatment and open-faced female dog rings for rapid shift response. No explicit founding mission or differentiator statement beyond the technical specifications is provided.
